open-question.question: In the Settings window of Gurita for VS Code, a line switched to another harness takes that harness's first listed model and keeps its effort or takes the harness's first listed one, and today the switch is refused with an error when that harness's model list or effort list is empty. The harness dropdown is to offer Codex, whose model list and new effort list hold only the values that recipe lines and the person's own additions carry, so either list can be empty, while a Codex line can also run at the account's defaults with no model and no effort written. What happens when a line is switched to Codex while Codex's model list or effort list is empty?

recommendation.option: Require a model, omit an empty effort

open-question.recommendation: An empty effort list, the state of a fresh install, no longer blocks the switch, while every line the switch writes carries `-m` and so keeps its model and harness dropdowns and its way back, under the unchanged rule that a pick inserts no text; a model list emptied by hand still gets today's refusal, which says why.

alternative.id: Require a model, omit an empty effort

open-question.alternative: The two lists are treated differently: an empty model list still refuses the switch with today's error notification, while an empty effort list lets the switch go ahead with no effort override written, so the line runs at the account's default effort. A non-empty effort list gives the kept or first effort as decided. Picks still insert no text, so a Codex line written without the override has no effort dropdown until the flag is written by hand. Every Codex line the switch writes carries `-m`, which is what gives a Codex line its controls today, so the line keeps its model dropdown and its harness dropdown, while the new effort list, the one most likely to be empty, no longer blocks the switch. The rule is asymmetric and has to be explained, a switch is still blocked while the model list is empty, and a line written without the effort override cannot have its effort picked from the window later without a hand edit.

The switch to Codex keeps today's behaviour for an empty list: `rewriteHarness` refuses an offer listing no model or no effort, the Settings window tells it in its existing error notification (`The harness could not be changed: …`), and the line is left as it stands. The Codex option stays offered in the dropdown whatever its lists hold, and the person adds a model or an effort under Models and efforts before switching again. Nothing new is written for a Codex line with no model or no effort. No new code path: the existing refusal in `rewriteHarness` and `editLineHarness` already covers Codex once it is switchable, every Codex line the switch writes carries `-m` and the effort override and so always gets its model and effort dropdowns, and a switch back to Claude Code or Antigravity always has values to map. The dropdown offers a choice that fails only after it is picked, and while Codex's lists are empty (likely for the new effort list, filled only by Codex lines carrying the override) the switch is unusable until the person types entries by hand; whether the lists are empty in practice depends on what the shipped Codex line carries.

alternative.id: Disable Codex while a list is empty

open-question.alternative: The line's harness dropdown shows Codex as a disabled entry while Codex's model list or effort list is empty, its hover text naming the empty list and pointing at Models and efforts, so no switch to Codex reaches the host; once both lists hold an entry Codex is picked normally and takes the first model and the kept or first effort as decided. The host keeps `rewriteHarness`'s refusal as a guard behind it. Nothing is written for a Codex line with no model or no effort. The person learns why Codex cannot be picked before trying, with no error after a click, and every Codex line the switch writes still carries both values and so keeps both dropdowns and a switch back. The Settings page script must receive and track Codex's list state per line's dropdown and redraw it as the lists change, and the switch is still blocked whenever a list is empty, so a person content with the account's defaults must first invent an entry they do not want.

alternative.id: Omit the flag of an empty list

open-question.alternative: The switch always succeeds: for each of the two lists, a non-empty list gives its value as decided (the first model as `-m`, the kept or first effort as `-c model_reasoning_effort=<level>`), and an empty list gives no flag at all, so the line runs at the account's default model, default effort, or both. The rule that a model or effort pick inserts no text into a line stays, so a Codex line left without `-m` gets no model dropdown and one left without the override no effort dropdown until the flag is written by hand, and the existing refusal is removed for the Codex switch. Codex can be picked at once whatever its lists hold, and the line it writes is the account-defaults form a Codex line can legitimately take, with no invented value standing in it. A line written without a flag loses that value's control in the Settings window, and since today's line editor gives a Codex line controls only when it carries `-m`, a line written with no model shows as read-only text with no harness dropdown, so it cannot be switched back or given a model from the window even after the lists gain entries.

The switch always succeeds and writes no flag for an empty list, as in omitting the flag, and in addition a Codex line gets its harness, model, and effort controls whether or not it carries `-m` or the effort override: each dropdown opens on an "account default" entry standing for no flag, picking a listed value inserts `-m <model>` or `-c model_reasoning_effort=<level>` into the line's first command, and picking the default entry removes the flag. The module rule that a pick inserts no text is lifted for Codex lines, and a Codex line with no model or no effort can be switched back to Claude Code or Antigravity, taking that harness's first model and kept or first effort. Every Codex line, the account-defaults form included, stays fully editable from the Settings window, so an empty list never blocks the switch and never strands a line the switch wrote. The largest change: `lineValues.ts` gains flag insertion and removal, `lineEditor` and the page script gain a default entry and controls for flag-less lines, and the stored `custom N` variants and tests grow with them, all for a case that arises only while a list is empty.

When a list Codex's switch needs is empty, the host asks for the value in VS Code's own input box, the way the Settings window already asks for a list entry (one box per empty list, its validation refusing an empty entry), adds the typed value to Codex's list as the person's addition (`addedModels` or `addedEfforts`), and writes it into the line as decided; dismissing the box writes nothing, neither the line nor the list. A non-empty list is used without asking. The switch completes in one gesture with a real value the person chose, every Codex line written carries both flags and so keeps its dropdowns and a switch back, and the list is filled for every later switch. A dropdown pick opens a modal prompt the other switches never show, and the person must know a valid Codex model name or effort level to type, with no way through this path to say they want the account's default instead.

The extension ships a fixed default Codex model list and effort list (the effort list Codex's documented reasoning levels) laid beneath the values derived from recipe lines, so Codex's lists are never empty unless the person removes every entry through the existing `removedModels`/`removedEfforts` overlay; the switch takes the first listed model and the kept or first effort as decided, and a list the person has emptied refuses as today. The switch works out of the box on a fresh install with no shipped or own Codex line, and every line it writes carries both values and keeps its controls. It reverses the recorded rule that the extension ships no list of its own and queries no harness, and a built-in model name goes stale as Codex's models change, needing a release to update while a stale first entry is what every switch writes; how much it adds depends on what the shipped Codex line carries.
